import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_83/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_83/test_1.csv"

# Load Source 0
# index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column as per hint 24
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Rename Source 0 columns to match target suffix _15 columns
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={
    'Happiness Rank': 'Happiness_Rank_15',
    'Happiness Score': 'Happiness_Score_15',
    'Standard Error': 'Standard_Error_15',
    'Economy (GDP per Capita)': 'Economy_15',
    'Health (Life Expectancy)': 'Life_Expectancy_15',
    'Trust (Government Corruption)': 'Trust_15',
    'Generosity': 'Generosity_15',
    'Dystopia Residual': 'Dystopia_15'
})

# Select and reorder columns from Source 0 to match target schema columns for 2015
df0_selected = df0_renamed[[
    'Country', 'Region', 'Happiness_Rank_15', 'Happiness_Score_15', 'Standard_Error_15',
    'Economy_15', 'Family', 'Life_Expectancy_15', 'Freedom', 'Trust_15',
    'Generosity_15', 'Dystopia_15'
]]

# Rename columns in df0_selected to exactly match target schema for 2015 columns
df0_selected = df0_selected.rename(columns={
    'Family': 'Family_15',
    'Freedom': 'Freedom_15'
})

# Load Source 1
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source 1 columns already mostly match target schema for 2017 columns
# Just ensure all columns exist and are in correct order for joining
# Columns in Source 1: ['Country', 'Happiness_Rank_17', 'Happiness_Score_17', 'Whisker_High_17', 'Whisker_Low_17',
#                       'Economy_17', 'Family_17', 'Life_Expectancy_17', 'Freedom_17', 'Generosity_17', 'Trust_17', 'Dystopia_17']

# Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'Country'
# Both have 'Country' column with many distinct values and overlap
# This join will combine 2015 and 2017 data side by side

# Before join, check for duplicates in 'Country' in both dfs to avoid many-to-many join
# If duplicates exist, drop duplicates keeping first occurrence (based on domain knowledge, countries should be unique)
df0_unique = df0_selected.drop_duplicates(subset=['Country'])
df1_unique = df1.drop_duplicates(subset=['Country'])

# Perform inner join on 'Country' to keep only countries present in both sources
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_unique, df1_unique, on='Country', how='inner')

# After join, ensure 'Region' column is present (from df0)
# Target schema expects 'Region' as second column
# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly

target_columns = [
    'Country', 'Region',
    'Happiness_Rank_15', 'Happiness_Score_15', 'Standard_Error_15', 'Economy_15', 'Family_15',
    'Life_Expectancy_15', 'Freedom_15', 'Trust_15', 'Generosity_15', 'Dystopia_15',
    'Happiness_Rank_17', 'Happiness_Score_17', 'Whisker_High_17', 'Whisker_Low_17', 'Economy_17',
    'Family_17', 'Life_Expectancy_17', 'Freedom_17', 'Generosity_17', 'Trust_17', 'Dystopia_17'
]

# Some countries might be missing in one source, so the join might reduce rows.
# This matches the target example count (75 rows), which is less than source0 (79) and source1 (155).

# Select and reorder columns
df_final = df_merged[target_columns]

# Convert data types to match target schema exactly
# Target schema types:
# 'Country': string
# 'Region': string
# 'Happiness_Rank_15': int
# 'Happiness_Score_15': float
# 'Standard_Error_15': float
# 'Economy_15': float
# 'Family_15': float
# 'Life_Expectancy_15': float
# 'Freedom_15': float
# 'Trust_15': float
# 'Generosity_15': float
# 'Dystopia_15': float
# 'Happiness_Rank_17': int
# 'Happiness_Score_17': float
# 'Whisker_High_17': float
# 'Whisker_Low_17': float
# 'Economy_17': float
# 'Family_17': float
# 'Life_Expectancy_17': float
# 'Freedom_17': float
# 'Generosity_17': float
# 'Trust_17': float
# 'Dystopia_17': float

# Convert string columns explicitly
df_final['Country'] = df_final['Country'].astype(str)
df_final['Region'] = df_final['Region'].astype(str)

# Convert integer columns
df_final['Happiness_Rank_15'] = df_final['Happiness_Rank_15'].astype(int)
df_final['Happiness_Rank_17'] = df_final['Happiness_Rank_17'].astype(int)

# Convert float columns
float_columns = [
    'Happiness_Score_15', 'Standard_Error_15', 'Economy_15', 'Family_15', 'Life_Expectancy_15',
    'Freedom_15', 'Trust_15', 'Generosity_15', 'Dystopia_15',
    'Happiness_Score_17', 'Whisker_High_17', 'Whisker_Low_17', 'Economy_17', 'Family_17',
    'Life_Expectancy_17', 'Freedom_17', 'Generosity_17', 'Trust_17', 'Dystopia_17'
]

for col in float_columns:
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].astype(float)

# Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_83/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
